reason: Two of the three parts hold on measurement; one holds only after its stated reason is thrown away. (1) ROW CONTROL - CONFIRMED. Measured in owner-flight, .b-date and .b-grab are byte-identical typography: Geist Mono, 11px, letter-spacing 1.76px, uppercase, rgba(255,255,255,0.62). The only rest-state difference is an 8px left offset that is invisible without a ground, and cursor:pointer, which is not a rest state. The screenshot confirms SAT 1 AUG and SHOWN are indistinguishable until hover, and hover does not exist on the phone frame. A control that only declares itself on hover is a real defect at 9.5 on the owner's primary object. (2) UNFURL DATE - CONFIRMED. .b-ogWho and .b-ogDate are both 11px mono uppercase at fore-62, separated by 2.2px vs 1.76px of tracking - a 0.44px difference, correctly described as imperceptible. The rendered card reads stamp / number / stamp, and DAYS TO SATURDAY 3 OCTOBER 2026 is the widest line on it. I built the proposed sans, sentence-case, fore-72 15px version and rendered it: the card gains two registers, the mono top line stays ceremonial, and the couple's date stops reading as a machine stamp. Real improvement, no constraint touched (Geist 400, no new hue). (3) 48 -> 64px - REASON REFUTED, CHANGE CONFIRMED ONLY AS A CONSEQUENCE OF (2). The stated justification is wrong arithmetic: the card is 298x156.4 and the app viewport is 1440x960, so 48px in the card is 27.6% of its frame height against 13.3% for the app's 148px count. The card does not invert the app's hierarchy; proportionally its numeral is already twice as dominant, and the number visibly dominates the current render. Judged on its own the raise is unearned. But rendered against the part-(2) caption, 48px loses the ratio - the brighter, larger sans line pulls level - and 64px restores it, with ~20px of slack left in the card (content 136px in a 156.4px box, no overflow). So take the raise as a consequence of (2), not on the reason given, and never on its own. Also refuted inside the fix: the fore-46 demotion of .b-grab. I applied it and ran the audit gate - it passes contrast (measured 4.68:1 composited over #111111, above 4.5), so it is not a gate break, but it makes the only pressable thing in the row the dimmest text on it, which inverts affordance to buy affordance. The underline alone does the work; the ink drop is a trade of one defect for another.
sharpenedFix: Three separate edits in b.css, in this order. (1) .b-grab: KEEP color: var(--fore-62). Add only text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-color: var(--fore-16); text-underline-offset: 3px; text-decoration-thickness: 1px. Verified render: the word reads as a control at rest without losing ink to the date beside it, and the existing hover/focus promotion to var(--fore) plus the fore-06 ground still lands. Drop the color: var(--fore-46) clause entirely. Check the underline does not leak into any audience or print state before merging - .b-grab renders only when o.owner is true, so it should not, but confirm on the print and phone frames. If the underline reads too much like a link for a state toggle, the alternative is a resting ground (background: var(--fore-04)) with no ink change; do not do both. (2) .b-ogDate: font-family: var(--sans); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.4; letter-spacing: var(--track-body); text-transform: none; color: var(--fore-72). Leave the string produced in render-b.js line 656 as 'days to ' + F.fmt.longYear(...) - the fix text quotes '79 days to Saturday 3 October 2026', but the 79 is .b-ogNum, a separate element; do not fold the numeral into the caption. Sentence case falls out of removing text-transform, so no JS change is needed. (3) .b-ogNum: 48px -> 64px with letter-spacing: var(--track-display). Ship this ONLY together with (2); if (2) is rejected, leave the numeral at 48px, because the stated 48-vs-148 justification is measurement across two different frames and does not stand alone. After (3), re-check the card against a longer project date and a two-line project name for wrap before signing off.
